Compliance · US

Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program

FedRAMP Rev. 5 security control baselines (NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5); FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026 · active; Rev. 5 baselines and FedRAMP 20x (consolidated rules for 2026) · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Cloud service offerings used by US federal agencies (Rev. 5 certifications and the 20x path under the Consolidated Rules for 2026).

A check shows a breach in code; it does not certify that a point is met. List scraped from the publisher's document on 2026-11-01, the publisher's document on 2026-11-01, the publisher's document on 2026-11-01. A point here means: The controls and enhancements of FedRAMP's Rev. 5 High, Moderate, Low and LI-SaaS baselines (the publisher's Security Controls Baseline workbook), each with the SP 800-53 statement parts from NIST's OSCAL catalogue, which is what FedRAMP adopts. Discussion and guidance left out. Plus FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026 from the datafile the site publishes (version 2026.10.13.01): every ruleset, subset, rule, key security indicator and definition. Its CTL block (FedRAMP parameter values and guidance for Rev. 5 controls), rule notes, examples and following-information lists are left out: they refine points already listed..

IA-5a Verify identity of whoever receives an authenticator at initial distribution. Coming soon
IA-5b Establish initial content for authenticators the organisation issues. Coming soon
IA-5c Make sure authenticators are strong enough for their intended use. Coming soon
IA-5d Define procedures for distributing, replacing and revoking authenticators that are lost, compromised or damaged. Coming soon
IA-5e Change default authenticators before first use. We detect

secrets.insecure-defaultA sample signing secret in the env template or CI config is a well-known default authenticator; nothing makes a deployment change it before first use. (FedRAMP L,M,H)
IA-5f Change or refresh authenticators at defined intervals or on defined events. Coming soon
IA-5g Protect authenticator content from unauthorised disclosure and modification. We detect

secrets.committedEveryone with read access to the repository, its clones and forks can read the credential, so its content is disclosed. (FedRAMP L,M,H)

secrets.in-historyAnyone who clones the repository can recover the credential from history, so its content is not protected from disclosure. (FedRAMP L,M,H)
IA-5h Require people and devices to apply specific controls protecting authenticators. Coming soon
IA-5i Change group or role account authenticators when membership changes. Coming soon
IA-5(1) Password-based AuthenticationPassword-based authentication requirements follow.
IA-5(1)(a) Keep and update a list of common or compromised passwords. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(b) Check new passwords against the list of common or compromised passwords. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(c) Send passwords only over cryptographically protected channels. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(d) Store passwords with an approved salted key derivation function. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(e) Force a new password to be chosen right after account recovery. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(f) Let users choose long passwords and passphrases with any printable characters. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(g) Provide automated tools helping users choose strong passwords. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(h) Enforce defined password composition and complexity rules. Coming soon
IA-5(2) Public Key-based Authentication
IA-5(2)(a) Public key authentication requirements follow.
IA-5(2)(a)(1) Enforce authorised access to the corresponding private key. Coming soon
IA-5(2)(a)(2) Map the authenticated key identity to the individual's or group's account. Coming soon
IA-5(2)(b) Requirements that apply when PKI is used.
IA-5(2)(b)(1) Validate certificate paths to a trust anchor, including revocation status checks. We detect

tls.verification-disabledTurning verification off skips certification path validation of the peer's certificate. (FedRAMP M,H)
IA-5(2)(b)(2) Keep a local cache of revocation data for path validation. Coming soon
IA-5(6) Protection of AuthenticatorsProtect authenticators in line with the sensitivity of what they unlock. Coming soon
IA-5(7) No Embedded Unencrypted Static AuthenticatorsDo not embed unencrypted static authenticators in applications or static storage. We detect

arch.privileged-key-client-sideThe privileged key is inlined into the client bundle, an unencrypted static authenticator embedded in the application. (FedRAMP M,H)

secrets.committedA credential committed in plain text is an unencrypted static authenticator embedded in the application's static storage. (FedRAMP M,H)

secrets.in-historyThe credential stays embedded in the repository's static storage (its history) even after it was removed from the working tree. (FedRAMP M,H)
IA-5(8) Multiple System AccountsApply defined safeguards against risk from individuals holding accounts on multiple systems. Coming soon
IA-5(13) Expiration of Cached AuthenticatorsBlock use of cached authenticators after a defined period. Coming soon

KSI-CMT-VTD Validating Throughout DeploymentTesting and validation of changes during deployment is automated. We detect

agent.as02.neutralised-checkA check forced to always pass provides no real automated validation of changes, directly contradicting the requirement.

ci.missingNo pipeline runs the gate, which is direct evidence that changes are not being tested automatically during delivery.

ci.nonblocking-checksTest, lint or security steps cannot fail the build, so automated validation has no effect on whether changes proceed.

KSI-SVC-ACM Automating Configuration ManagementResource configuration is automated and reviewed for drift. Coming soon
KSI-SVC-ASM Automating Secret ManagementManagement, protection and rotation of keys, certificates and secrets is automated and reviewed. We detect

secrets.committedLive secret material sitting in tracked files is concrete evidence that keys and credentials are not being protected.
KSI-SVC-EIS Evaluating and Improving SecurityResources are continually evaluated for security improvements, which are then made. Coming soon
KSI-SVC-PRR Preventing Residual RiskAfter changes, plans and resource state are reviewed to remove unwanted residual elements. Coming soon
KSI-SVC-RUD Removing Unwanted DataUnwanted federal customer data is removed promptly on agency request, including from backups. Coming soon
KSI-SVC-SIN Securing InformationInformation is encrypted or otherwise protected against unwanted access or modification. We detect

db.sensitive-column-plaintextCard, identifier or health columns show no protection, which is direct evidence that stored data lacks required safeguarding.

KSI-SVC-VCM Validating CommunicationsAuthenticity and integrity of communications between resources is validated using automation. We detect

tls.verification-disabledSkipping certificate checks means the peer's identity goes unverified on machine connections, directly failing the required validation.

FRD-VLR Vulnerability ResponseDefines the process of tracking, evaluating, mitigating, remediating and reporting detected vulnerabilities. Coming soon

Reuse: US government publication on an official .gov site; reuse terms on the publisher's site (not re-checked); cite IDs and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Slop to pop: design patterns: anti-patterns sloptopop converts into design patterns today, with the run that proves each one.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.

This site runs no JavaScript except htmx on the pricing page, to send the waitlist form; every animation is CSS. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
